title: Maximum Area Rectangle With Point Constraints I
statement:
Each entry `points[i] = [x, y]` is a distinct point of the plane. Look at rectangles whose sides are parallel to the axes and whose four corners are all points from `points`. Such a rectangle counts only if no other point of `points` lies inside it or on its boundary.

Return the largest area of a rectangle that counts, or `-1` if there is none.
constraints: 0 <= x, y <= 100 for every point [x, y]
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 10 points, enumeration is cheap. An axis-parallel rectangle is fixed by two opposite corners: a bottom-left corner `(x1, y1)` and a top-right corner `(x2, y2)` force the other two corners to be `(x1, y2)` and `(x2, y1)`. So try every pair of points as that diagonal, look the two missing corners up in a set, and then scan all points to make sure nothing else touches the rectangle. (The brute force instead tries every group of four points.)

## Approach

1. Put every point into `seen` as a string `key`, so a corner lookup takes O(1).
2. For each pair `(x1, y1)`, `(x2, y2)`, skip it unless `x1 < x2` and `y1 < y2`. The pair is then the bottom-left and top-right corners, so each rectangle is examined once.
3. Skip it unless `seen` holds both `(x1, y2)` and `(x2, y1)`.
4. Count the points in the closed box from `(x1, y1)` to `(x2, y2)`. The four corners are always counted, so `inside === 4` means no other point is inside or on the border.
5. Keep the largest valid area in `best`, which stays `-1` when no rectangle qualifies.

## Example 1, step by step

Only the pair `(1, 1)`, `(3, 3)` passes step 2. Both `(1, 3)` and `(3, 1)` are in `seen`, and the box holds just the four corners, so `inside = 4` and `best = (3 - 1) · (3 - 1) = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n³): n² pairs, each checked with an O(n) scan.
- Space: O(n) for the set.

## Pitfalls

- Ignoring points on the border: a point on an edge, even between two corners, makes the rectangle invalid.
- Comparing the count with 0: the four corners are in the box too, so a clean rectangle has `inside === 4`.
- Returning 0 instead of `-1` when no rectangle qualifies.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `seen` | every point as an `"x,y"` string |
| `x1`, `y1` | the bottom-left corner |
| `x2`, `y2` | the top-right corner |
| `inside` | points in the closed rectangle, corners included |
| `best` | largest valid area so far, or `-1` |

narration.2: Turn a point into a string so a set can look it up.
narration.3: Store every point for constant-time corner lookups.
narration.4: -1 means no valid rectangle has been found yet.
narration.6: Try each point as the bottom-left corner...
narration.7: ...and each point as the top-right corner.
narration.8: The second point must lie strictly right of and above the first; this also visits each rectangle once.
narration.11: The other two corners are forced; both must be among the points.
narration.14: Count the points in the closed rectangle, border included.
narration.16: Is this point inside the rectangle or on its border?
narration.20: Only the four corners lie in it, so the rectangle is valid.
narration.25: The largest valid area, or -1 if no rectangle qualified.
